analysis: The PR changes only docs/operations/provider-release.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and a new sentence block near line 204 saying that a pull-request run on a Darkbloom Sandbox with no Darkbloom cache skips every cache step of .github/actions/provider-release-build and builds cold, while the release workflows never skip them. The edit is documentation only. It changes no code, workflow, secret handling, signing, registration or publication logic, and it alters none of the documented controls. Those controls are the tag-gated prod signing identity, the PROD_*/DEV_* secret separation, the signing keychain removal, the hash-pinned registration, and the qualification and revocation gates tied to T-052/T-054. The new text is consistent with the surrounding statement that the PR-scoped cache lanes hold no signing or publication secrets. It also does not weaken the documented assumption that a cache hit does not authorize publication. A cold build skipping cache steps affects build speed and availability only; it does not skip signing or verification. Remaining integration questions: whether the actual action.yml implements the described skip condition, and whether the 'release workflows never skip' claim holds. Neither file is in the supplied evidence, so they are unverified. Nothing in this docs-only diff creates a concrete security regression. The threat model needs no update on this evidence.
